title: Summer Haircuts for Hot, Dry Weather
hero_alt: Young man in sunglasses with short sides, smiling outdoors on a sunny day
card_text: Short sides, a top that needs nothing, and a scalp that still needs covering. Three cuts built for a Carlsbad summer.
lede: For a hot, dry summer, go shorter on the sides and simpler on top. Less hair means less heat trapped against your head, less sweat sitting in it, and less styling on mornings when it's already warm by breakfast. A buzz cut, a skin fade or a short textured crop all do that, each with a different amount left on top.
Here's how to pick between them, what a shorter cut means for your scalp in the New Mexico sun, and how to fit a cut around summer days.

blocks.heading: Less hair, less work.
blocks.lead: Carlsbad summers are hot and dry.
paragraphs: Thick sides hold heat close to the head and soak up sweat. Taking them short lets air reach the skin and lets your hair dry fast after you've been outside.

The top is the other half of the decision. Anything you have to blow-dry or set every morning becomes a chore when the temperature climbs, and product and sweat don't mix well. A summer cut should look right with a rinse and a towel.
Short doesn't have to mean plain. A sharp line-up, a clean neckline or a fade with real contrast keeps a low-effort cut looking deliberate.

blocks.heading: Pick your length.
blocks.lead: From almost nothing to a little texture.

subsections.heading: Buzz cut
paragraphs: One short length all over, or close to it. Nothing to style, quick to dry and easy to wear under a cap. The photo above takes it a step further, with a high fade on the sides and a sharp line-up across the front.

subsections.heading: Skin fade
paragraphs: Sides taken down to bare skin and blended up into whatever length you keep on top. The coolest-feeling sides you can get without shaving them.

subsections.heading: Textured crop
paragraphs: A short top with choppy texture, pushed forward, over short sides. Enough hair to look styled, little enough that a towel-dry and your fingers handle it.

blocks.heading: Shorter hair, more sun.
paragraphs: The shorter the cut, the less your hair shades your scalp. A buzz cut or a high skin fade leaves skin open to the sun that used to sit under hair, including along the part and around the crown.
Treat that skin the way you'd treat your face on a bright day outside. Shade and a hat help, and the back of the neck deserves the same attention once a fade has bared it.
If you're going very short for the first time this summer, expect the skin on top to be lighter than the rest of you for a while. That evens out on its own.

items.q: What's a good haircut for hot weather?
items.a: Something short on the sides and easy on top: a buzz cut, a skin fade or a short textured crop.

items.q: Does a shorter haircut keep you cooler?
items.a: Shorter sides let air reach your scalp and let sweat dry faster, which is why most summer cuts start there.

items.q: Should I shave my head for summer?
items.a: You can. The Head & Beard Shave takes both down smooth. Keep in mind a bare scalp gets full sun, so plan to cover it.
